articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender weakness dubbed 'BlueHammer' — because apparently April showers bring May CVEs. Chrome also patched its fourth critical this year, proving browser security is as reliable as a chocolate teapot.

articles.title: Trellix Confirms Source Code Breach With Unauthorized Repository Access
articles.summary: CISA adds CVE-2026-31431 to its KEV catalog as attackers exploit a Linux root access bug in the wild. When CISA says 'patch now,' they mean yesterday — unless you enjoy unauthorized root parties on your servers.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vuln gets weaponized with ransomware attacks hitting 'millions' of potentially exposed sites. One of the internet's most widely used hosting stacks just became a highway to hell for web admins.

articles.title: 30,000 Facebook Accounts Hacked via Google AppSheet Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Cybersecurity company Trellix admits to source code breach because apparently even the security vendors can't secure themselves. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a compromised private key.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: ALPR surveillance networks exposed through public records requests are now triggering state laws to hide what citizens can see. When transparency reveals mass surveillance, governments suddenly discover a passion for privacy — their own.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new anti-VPN law goes live next week, because nothing says 'freedom' like criminalizing basic privacy tools. Watch VPN usage surge as residents scramble to maintain anonymity — it's almost like prohibition never works.

articles.title: Five Eyes spook shops warn rapid rollouts of agentic AI are too risky
articles.summary: FBI redirects 9,000 personnel to immigration enforcement under Trump's deportation push, potentially compromising national security. Because apparently hunting immigrants is more important than actual threats — priorities, people.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after their 2022 SMS phishing spree. Another young hacker learns that cybercrime doesn't pay — at least not in the way they expected.

articles.title: A Bridge to Somewhere: How to Link Your Mastodon, Bluesky, or Other Federated Accounts
articles.summary: Germany doxes 'UNKN,' the elusive mastermind behind REvil and GandCrab ransomware gangs, revealing 31-year-old Russian Daniil Shchukin. Turns out even the most mysterious ransomware kingpins eventually get their close-up.

articles.title: If AI's So Smart, Why Does It Keep Deleting Production Databases?
articles.summary: North Korea now controls 76% of all stolen crypto in 2026, turning cybercrime into a state-sponsored revenue stream. Kim Jong Un's hackers are apparently better at crypto than most day traders — and infinitely more successful at HODLing.
